stories.headline: Alibaba Q4 Revenue Up 3% to $35.3B, Cloud Up 38% as AI Spend Pressures Margins

key_facts.fact: Alibaba reported quarterly revenue of RMB243.38 billion ($35.28B) for the three months ended March 31, 2026, up 3% year-over-year from RMB236.45B; on a like-for-like basis (excluding divested Sun Art and Intime), revenue would have grown 11%.
Cloud Intelligence Group revenue rose 38% YoY to RMB41.63 billion ($6.04B), the headline AI-driven growth line.
Quick commerce revenue jumped 57% to RMB19.99 billion as Alibaba leans into 'Taobao Instant Commerce' and Ele.me.
Pre-earnings analyst consensus was $35.81B revenue and $1.02 EPS, a sharp drop from the $1.57 reported in March 2025; the December quarter had missed by 48.57%.
BABA shares were down about 9% year-to-date heading into the print as investors weighed AI capex against profitability.

stories.headline: Anduril Raises $5B Series H at $61B, Doubling Valuation in Under a Year

key_facts.fact: Anduril Industries raised a $5 billion Series H led by Thrive Capital and Andreessen Horowitz at a $61 billion valuation.
The new valuation roughly doubles the $30.5 billion mark set in Anduril's June 2025 Series G, which raised $2.5 billion.
The Series H brings Anduril's total funding to $6.82 billion; the company is reportedly weighing an IPO as soon as 2027.
Initial reports in March 2026 had Anduril seeking $4 billion at a $60 billion valuation, with potential to bring in as much as $8 billion of capital.

stories.headline: Anthropic in Talks to Raise $30B–$50B at Up to $950B Valuation

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is in talks to raise between $30 billion and $50 billion in a round that would value it at up to $950 billion.

Bloomberg reports the talks involve at least $30 billion in fresh financing at a valuation of more than $900 billion, not including the new investment, with the round potentially closing by month-end.
The talks come less than three months after Anthropic's $30 billion round closed in February 2026 at a $380 billion valuation.
Anthropic's annualized revenue has reached $30 billion, up from roughly $10 billion in 2025 and $9 billion at the end of 2025.
A $950B valuation would surpass OpenAI's most recent public round at $852 billion post-money in late March 2026.

stories.headline: Anthropic Launches 12 Claude Legal Plugins and MCP Connectors for Law Firms

key_facts.fact: Anthropic announced a dozen new Claude plugins targeted at attorneys, law students and others in the legal sector, including a 'commercial counsel' tool aimed at vendor agreement review and a study tool for the bar exam.

The 12 plugins span commercial, privacy, corporate, employment, product and AI governance, covering document search/review, case-law research, deposition preparation and drafting; they include 'employment counsel', 'litigation associate' and a 'law student' bar-exam tool.

Anthropic also released MCP connectors that link Claude to leading legal software platforms, including Thomson Reuters' Westlaw and Practical Law, Box for document management, Everlaw for e-discovery and Docusign for e-signature.
All twelve plugins are available to existing paying Claude customers and can run inside Claude Cowork or be embedded into a firm's existing systems.

stories.headline: Anthropic in Advanced Talks to Buy SDK Generator Stainless for $300M+

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is in advanced talks to acquire New York-based Stainless, a startup that helps developers generate SDKs from APIs, for at least $300 million.
Stainless's SDK-generation software is currently used by Anthropic's rivals, including OpenAI and Google; OpenAI adopted Stainless after struggling to maintain its own SDK.
Stainless has also built dedicated software linking with Model Context Protocol (MCP), the standard Anthropic launched in November 2024.

The deal would extend a six-month M&A run for Anthropic following the December 2025 acquisition of developer-tools startup Bun and subsequent purchases of computer-use startup Vercept and AI biotech startup Coefficient Bio.

stories.headline: Google DeepMind Unveils Gemini-Powered 'Magic Pointer' for Chrome and Googlebook

key_facts.fact: Google DeepMind published a research blog and experimental demos for an AI-enabled mouse pointer powered by Gemini that aims to understand both what the user is pointing at and why it matters.
Two interactive demos are live in Google AI Studio: one for editing images by pointing and talking, and one for finding places on a map.

The pointer is being integrated into Gemini in Chrome — users can select products on a page and ask Gemini to compare, or point to visualize a new couch in their living room — and into the upcoming 'Googlebook' laptop as 'Magic Pointer'.

Google announced the Magic Pointer alongside Googlebook, a new laptop category 'built from the ground up for Gemini intelligence' set to launch in fall 2026, in partnership with OEMs including Dell and HP.

stories.headline: Foxconn Confirms North America Factory Cyberattack; Nitrogen Claims 8TB Stolen

key_facts.fact: Foxconn confirmed Tuesday that some of its North American factories suffered a cyberattack and that affected plants are 'currently resuming normal production' after outages.

Ransomware group Nitrogen claimed responsibility, posting that it stole 8 terabytes of data — roughly 11 million files — including schematics and project details from Dell, Google, Apple, AMD, Intel, and Nvidia.

The breach centered on Foxconn's Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin facility — a hub for AI server production — where Wi-Fi was cut off May 1 and core plant infrastructure was disrupted; production was halted for roughly a week before resuming May 12.
Allegedly stolen materials include data center network topology diagrams for Google and Intel — architectural maps of live infrastructure with supply chain intelligence implications.

stories.headline: Foxconn Confirms Cyberattack on North American Factories; Nitrogen Ransomware Claims 8TB Theft

key_facts.fact: Foxconn confirmed Tuesday May 12 that some of its North American factories suffered a cyberattack and affected facilities are resuming normal production
The Nitrogen ransomware group claimed to have stolen 8 TB of data and more than 11 million files from Foxconn
Nitrogen claims the leaks include confidential instructions, project documentation, and technical drawings tied to Intel, Apple, Google, Dell, AMD and Nvidia projects
The Wisconsin Mount Pleasant facility began experiencing Wi-Fi issues May 1 and core plant infrastructure was disrupted; production was interrupted for roughly a week
Foxconn operates factories in Wisconsin, Ohio, Texas, Virginia, Indiana and several locations across Mexico; the company declined to specify how many were impacted
Nitrogen, active since 2023, is believed to use code derived from the leaked Conti 2 builder and follows a double-extortion model

stories.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Reverses, Joins Trump on China Trip After 11th-Hour Invite

key_facts.fact: Nvidia confirmed CEO Jensen Huang would visit Beijing with Trump after the U.S. president personally called him; Huang flew to Alaska to board Air Force One during a refueling stop.
The reversal followed reports that Huang had been left off the original White House delegation list of 17 executives released Monday, a smaller group than the 27 who joined Trump's 2017 China trip.
Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk also traveled on Air Force One; Trump is scheduled to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday and Friday.

Huang's addition revived hopes of progress on Nvidia's stalled sale of H200 AI chips in China; Washington currently lets Nvidia sell the H200 with a 25% revenue surcharge to the U.S. Treasury, with more advanced chips still restricted.
Huang has previously pegged the China AI chip market at $50 billion and told CNBC last week it 'would be a privilege' to accompany Trump.

stories.headline: Isomorphic Labs Raises $2.1B Series B Led by Thrive to Scale AI Drug Design

key_facts.fact: Isomorphic Labs, a DeepMind spinout, raised $2.1 billion in a Series B led by Thrive Capital, with Alphabet, GV, MGX, Temasek, CapitalG, and the UK Sovereign AI Fund participating.
The new capital brings Isomorphic Labs' total external funding to roughly $2.7 billion across two rounds, both led by Thrive Capital.
CEO Demis Hassabis said the capital will scale the company's IsoDDE drug design engine and pipeline; the firm now expects first clinical trials by end of 2026, a delay from his earlier 2025 target.
Isomorphic Labs was founded in 2021 as a DeepMind spinout, building on AlphaFold; it previously signed drug discovery deals worth up to $3 billion with Eli Lilly and Novartis.

stories.headline: Trump Calls Jensen Huang Last-Minute to Join China Trip, Reviving Hopes for H200 Sales

key_facts.fact: Trump called Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on May 12 after seeing media coverage of his absence from the delegation, asking him to join the China trip
Huang flew to Alaska to board Air Force One during the trip's refueling stopover, joining Trump's flight to Beijing
Huang did not appear on an initial White House list of executives, which included Tesla's Elon Musk and Apple's Tim Cook
Huang's late addition is fueling hopes in China for a deal on Nvidia's stalled effort to sell H200 AI chips to local customers
Trump posted on Truth Social that he will ask President Xi to 'open up' China for U.S. businesses as his 'first request' during the summit
Huang has previously pegged China's market for AI chips at $50 billion and told CNBC last week it 'would be a privilege' to accompany Trump

stories.headline: NAND Contract Prices Up 600%+ and DRAM Up ~400% Since Late September 2025 on AI Buildout

key_facts.fact: Contract prices for NAND chips are up 600%+ since late September 2025, while DRAM contract prices are up ~400%, with analysts expecting further gains
Bernstein analyst Mark Li reported overall DRAM contract prices in April were 57% higher versus Q1, with server DRAM up 48%, mobile up ~80%, and consumer up ~60%
NAND contract prices are indicated to rise 65-70% quarter-on-quarter in 2Q 2026, driven primarily by SSD and mobile NAND packages
TrendForce projects PC DDR5 DRAM prices to rise 43-48% in Q2 2026, while DDR4 prices are expected to rise 35-40%
Bernstein flagged spot prices sent mixed signals — server DDR5 module spot prices down 6.7% MoM and NAND wafer spot prices fell ~7% as OEMs reduce purchases
Demand for server DRAM and eSSD remains robust, keeping supply tight, but price increases are expected to decelerate notably into Q3 2026

stories.headline: Photonic Closes $200M+ Round at $2B Valuation, Backed by Mubadala, Microsoft, RBC, Bell

key_facts.fact: Vancouver-based quantum computing startup Photonic announced the final close of over $200M USD ($275M CAD) in funding, hitting a $2B USD post-money valuation
The round was led by UK-based sustainable technology firm Planet First Partners, with new investors BDC, Export Development Canada, Bell Ventures, Firgun Ventures, and InBC Investment Corp
Photonic added $70M to its initial $130M January raise to complete the financing, bringing total capital raised to over $350M USD
Photonic's 'Entanglement First' architecture uses optically-linked silicon spin qubits, allowing fault-tolerant quantum systems to scale over existing fiber and telecom infrastructure
Other backers include the UK government's National Security Strategic Investment Fund and Canadian financiers Inovia Capital and Yaletown Partners
Photonic has more than 160 employees and is led by former video game executive Don Mattrick, with previous CEO Paul Terry moving to chief product officer

stories.headline: Recursive Superintelligence Raises $650M+ at $4B for Self-Improving AI

key_facts.fact: Recursive Superintelligence has raised over $650 million from venture firms including Google Ventures (GV) and Greycroft, plus chipmakers Nvidia and AMD.

The round values the four-month-old London-incorporated company at $4 billion pre-money; the prior FT report in April pegged at least $500 million committed and noted oversubscription could push the total to $1 billion.

The founding team includes Richard Socher (former Salesforce chief scientist), Tim Rocktäschel (UCL professor and former director of Google DeepMind's Open-Endedness group), and former OpenAI researchers Josh Tobin, Jeff Clune, and Tim Shi, with about 20 staff overall.
The company's stated goal is to automate the entire AI development pipeline — evaluation, data selection, training, post-training, and research direction — without human intervention at each step.

stories.headline: Samsung Pay Talks Collapse After 17 Hours; 50,000+ Workers Set to Strike May 21 for 18 Days

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics and its largest union failed to reach a pay deal after more than 17 hours of marathon talks that ended early Wednesday May 13
More than 50,000 unionized workers are expected to strike for 18 days starting May 21, threatening AI chip production
The union demands the abolition of the 50%-of-base-salary cap on bonus pay and the allocation of 15% of annual operating profit to the bonus pool
South Korean Prime Minister Kim Min-seok called an emergency meeting of related ministers, citing the 'gravity of the impact on the national economy'
A walkout could delay shipments to customers, push up chip prices further and benefit rivals such as SK Hynix
The union grievance centers on the bonus gap with rival SK Hynix; union representative Choi Seung-ho said no agenda items were addressed

stories.headline: SoftBank Q4 Net Profit Triples to $11.6B as OpenAI Stake Gains Hit $45B

key_facts.fact: SoftBank Group's Q4 (Jan–Mar 2026) net profit attributable jumped to 1.829 trillion yen ($11.61B) from 517.18B yen a year ago, well above Bloomberg estimates of 295.2B yen.
The result was driven by a 3.043 trillion yen gain on investments during the quarter, with the bulk from the Vision Funds.
SoftBank's OpenAI stake was valued at $79.6 billion as of end-March, representing a cumulative gain of $45 billion on the initial investment.
SoftBank still has $17.5 billion outstanding on a $40 billion bridge loan taken to fund its OpenAI commitments; cumulative invested capital is $34.6 billion.
SoftBank previously committed a further $30 billion in OpenAI in three $10B tranches through October 2026, which will bring its cumulative OpenAI investment to $64.6B and ownership to ~13%.

stories.headline: xAI Added 19 Gas Turbines to Colossus 2 in Past Two Months Despite Clean Air Act Lawsuit

key_facts.fact: Internal emails show xAI added 19 natural gas turbines at its Colossus 2 data center campus in Southhaven, Mississippi over the past two months
xAI is fighting a lawsuit filed by NAACP in April alleging Clean Air Act violations from operating unpermitted gas turbines
The original NAACP complaint cited 27 unpermitted gas turbines with 495 MW of generating capacity
A May 6 preliminary injunction filing claims up to 33 unpermitted gas turbines are now at the site, with only 14 equipped with emission controls
The Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality approved a Prevention of Significant Deterioration permit for 41 turbines at the site in March
